what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued the Pond View Commons 40B hearing to October 26, with November 9 named as a possible next date.
The board voted by voice to table traffic until consultant estimates are gathered, have staff identify peer-review consultants, and require agreed funds deposited first.
The fee waiver question was postponed while the board gathers fees paid by prior 40B projects and estimates its own processing costs.
No decision was made on waiving water and sewer district requirements; the board will seek feedback from the water district and Sewer Commission and review the intermunicipal agreements.
Peer-review selection for traffic, civil and fire will be handled in public on October 26, after the first case.

why_it_matters: The fee the developer pays, and who funds the outside traffic, civil and fire reviews, decides how much of the cost of reviewing a 200-unit project falls on the developer rather than the town budget.

Whether the Zoning Board of Appeals can waive water and sewer district requirements is unresolved, and it bears on whether the project connects to systems that residents and town meeting have planned and paid for, and on the long-term pump and storage costs the water superintendent raised.

The board voted on a special permit to build a new three-bedroom home on a nonconforming lot at 451 Townsend Harbor Road; the vote was not audible.
The board noted the Mass Ave applicant must still return for planning board site plan review and possibly Conservation Commission review.

why_it_matters: The Mass Ave permit sets the operating limits for a contractor yard near homes and schools, where neighbors raised noise, lighting and truck traffic.
The conditions are the enforceable part of the approval, and the planning board and possibly the Conservation Commission can still shape or change the project.

meetings.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals opened the public hearing on the Pond View Commons 40B comprehensive permit for 200 rental units on Howard Street. The Sewer Commission memo, town counsel's overview, the applicant's presentation and a long run of public comment, mostly opposed, covered sewer and water authority, traffic, environment and fees. The hearing was continued to October 12, with the applicant to file a written position and its traffic report beforehand.

budget_items.what_was_said: The Sewer Commission memo says the sewer department is funded entirely by an enterprise fund paid by sewer users and warned it could become insolvent if fees are waived.
The memo says the application misstates the sewer construction and permit fees for the project.
A speaker said the application puts the project cost and infrastructure costs at figures he called fictitious for running long water and sewer lines.
A speaker cited application page A11 comparing market and affordable rents for a three-bedroom unit and questioned affordability.
A Sewer Commission member said the connection fees the applicant seeks to waive would wipe out the sewer department's reserve capacity, and that the application's cost figures are inadequate.
The Sewer Commission member said privilege and connection fees go back to the town for connection and operating costs, including pump stations.
Leominster and Fitchburg charge by flow rather than metering, so leaks raise the town's costs.
Applicant's attorney said profit is limited and excess above the limit is due back to the town for affordable housing.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals opened its hearing on the Pond View Commons 40B comprehensive permit for 200 rental units on Howard Street, and continued it with no vote.
The Sewer Commission memo was read into the record; it says the sewer department is funded by user fees and could become insolvent if fees are waived.
A Sewer Commission member said the connection fees the applicant seeks to waive would use up the sewer department's reserve capacity.
Most public comment opposed the project, citing Howard Street traffic, runoff, schools, and the board's lack of authority to expand water and sewer districts.
The hearing was continued to October 12; the applicant is to file a written position on water and sewer authority and its traffic report beforehand.

why_it_matters: Whether sewer connection fees are waived bears on the sewer enterprise fund, which is paid by sewer users, so the outcome could reach sewer bills.
A 40B permit can override local zoning, so the October 12 session on water and sewer authority is where residents can see how far the board's power reaches.
